description: The canon's enforcement layer. session-start.ps1 injects the hard invariants, but only in a repository that has adopted the canon (an .sza-canon.json stamp at the repo root) - self-limiting, so an unrelated project never pays for it. The guards and the prompt-submit advisories are deliberately NOT self-limiting: each enforces a property of the operating system or the harness, not of a project's conventions, so they apply wherever the plugin is enabled. Every one of them is the hook the canon already asks for in prose (AI_USAGE.md sections 3 and 5, GITHUB_INTERACTION.md section 6) - a rules file states them at 1-8% compliance, a hook holds at ~99%. Escape hatch for all of them: SZA_HOOKS_OFF=1. The Bash and Read guards are wired behind a bash pre-filter so PowerShell is spawned only on a payload that could possibly trip them; the pre-filter may only skip calls the real check would have allowed.

hooks.command: input=$(cat); case "$input" in *find*) printf "%s" "$input" | pwsh -NoProfile -File "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/hooks/guard-find-command.ps1" ;; esac
input=$(cat); case "$input" in *.ps1*) printf "%s" "$input" | pwsh -NoProfile -File "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/hooks/guard-ps1-in-bash.ps1" ;; esac
input=$(cat); case "$input" in *'"limit"'*|*'"offset"'*) exit 0 ;; esac; printf "%s" "$input" | pwsh -NoProfile -File "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/hooks/guard-uncapped-read.ps1"
